why_winner: The opening two lines present the key comparison as a cold fact before any framing arrives — 13.6% vs 89%, no context needed, reader is already processing. Strongest hook of the three and the cleanest structure throughout. The allowed/blocked bullet lists make the practical implications scan faster than the prose equivalents in A or the numbered-list structure in B. Performance data supports this angle: comparison/split-screen hit 5.15% on the account's strongest Period 3 conversion post.

runner_up_notes.A: A's 'not because you're careless — because that's how attention works' is the most human-sounding line of the three. Worth noting for future posts on fatigue/attention themes.
runner_up_notes.B: B's numbered-list layer explanation (1. rules, 2. classifier) is clean but the overall register skews toward product announcement. The bold claim opener is strong; execution slightly too formal.

issues.description: The two-layers section in C uses 'Layer 1/Layer 2' as formal labels, which feel slightly mechanical for a LinkedIn audience used to plain prose.
issues.action: Simplify to: 'Your explicit allow/deny rules in settings.json run first. Deterministic. Absolute. / The classifier covers everything you didn't write a rule for.' — removes the label formality while keeping the logical sequence intact.
